description: Standing in the center of the square, the eye is drawn to the Ayuntamiento pavilion glowing under lantern light, its arcaded facade and clock tower rising over the uniform colonnade that rings the plaza. Lamplight washes the sandstone a deep gold, and the arcades stretch left and right in a perfect baroque rectangle. Plaza Mayor is called Spain's most beautiful square — at night, under the lanterns, it's easy to see why.

prompts.prompt-r1.txt: Photorealistic artistic interpretation of the Plaza Mayor in Salamanca, Spain, at night. View from the middle of the square facing the Ayuntamiento pavilion with its two small towers on the east side. Continuous three-storey arcaded Baroque facades in honey-coloured sandstone wrap the square on all four sides, with medallion balconies above the arcade level. Warm amber lantern lighting glows on the stone; the paved square is quiet with a few shuttered cafe terraces under the arcades. Deep blue-black night sky with thin cloud cover. Subject centred so it survives a 4:5 centre crop. No identifiable people prominent, no text or brand logos anywhere in the image. No on-image text at all.
